problem.passage:
Text 1
Botanists studying desert succulents have long noted that many species store large reserves of water in thick, fleshy leaves or stems, an adaptation widely credited with allowing these plants to survive months without rainfall. Researchers who favor this explanation point to the strong correlation between stem thickness and survival time during drought, arguing that water storage capacity is the single most important factor determining which succulent species persist in the driest habitats.

Text 2
Other botanists studying the same plants argue that water storage capacity alone cannot explain survival differences among succulent species with similarly thick stems. They point out that species vary considerably in how tightly they close their stomata, the small pores through which plants lose water vapor, during the hottest parts of the day. Species with stricter stomatal closure retained water far longer than similarly sized species with looser closure, suggesting that water conservation behavior, not just storage capacity, determines drought survival.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that water storage capacity is the single most important factor determining succulent survival in dry habitats?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Botanists studying desert succulents have long noted that many species store large reserves of water in thick, fleshy leaves or stems, an adaptation widely credited with allowing these plants to survive months without rainfall. Researchers who favor this explanation point to the strong correlation between stem thickness and survival time during drought, arguing that water storage capacity is the single most important factor determining which succulent species persist in the driest habitats.

Text 2
Other botanists studying the same plants argue that water storage capacity alone cannot explain survival differences among succulent species with similarly thick stems. They point out that species vary considerably in how tightly they close their stomata, the small pores through which plants lose water vapor, during the hottest parts of the day. Species with stricter stomatal closure retained water far longer than similarly sized species with looser closure, suggesting that water conservation behavior, not just storage capacity, determines drought survival.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that water storage capacity is the single most important factor determining succulent survival in dry habitats?
options: The author would agree, noting that species with thicker stems always closed their stomata more tightly than thinner species.
The author would argue that stomatal closure behavior can affect survival among species even when stem thickness is similar.
The author would argue that stem thickness has no relationship whatsoever to how long a succulent can survive drought.
The author would agree that storage capacity matters most, but only for succulents growing in sandy rather than rocky soils.
problem.explanation: Text 1은 줄기 두께와 가뭄 생존 기간 사이의 강한 상관관계를 근거로, 물 저장 능력이 사막 다육식물의 생존을 결정하는 가장 중요한 단일 요인이라고 주장한다. 반면 Text 2는 줄기 두께가 비슷한 종들 사이에서도 한낮에 기공을 얼마나 엄격히 닫는지에 따라 수분 보유 기간이 크게 달랐다는 관찰을 제시하며, 저장 능력만이 아니라 수분 보존 행동도 가뭄 생존을 결정한다고 주장한다. 따라서 Text 2의 저자는 줄기 두께가 비슷해도 기공 폐쇄 행동에 따라 생존이 달라질 수 있다고 반응할 것이다. B가 이를 정확히 반영하므로 정답은 B번이다. A는 Text 2가 제시한 독립적 요인(기공 폐쇄)을 줄기 두께와 항상 함께 나타나는 것처럼 뒤바꿔 말한 것(REVERSED_RELATIONSHIP), C는 Text 2가 하지 않은 극단적 주장인 줄기 두께가 생존과 전혀 무관하다는 입장을 잘못 귀속한 것(MISATTRIBUTED_STANCE), D는 지문에 없는 토양 유형 조건을 끌어들인 무관한 결합(IRRELEVANT_COMBINATION)이다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 argues that water storage capacity is the single most important factor in succulent drought survival, based on a strong correlation between stem thickness and survival time. Text 2, however, presents an observation that among species with similarly thick stems, those with stricter stomatal closure during the hottest parts of the day retained water far longer than those with looser closure, arguing that conservation behavior, not just storage capacity, matters. So the author of Text 2 would respond that stomatal closure behavior can affect survival even among species with similar stem thickness. Choice B captures this correctly, so B is correct. Choice A reverses the relationship by implying stomatal closure always accompanies thicker stems (REVERSED_RELATIONSHIP); choice C misattributes an extreme claim that stem thickness is irrelevant, which Text 2 never makes (MISATTRIBUTED_STANCE); choice D introduces a soil-type condition absent from both texts (IRRELEVANT_COMBINATION).
problem.evidenceTarget: Text 2는 Text 1이 강조한 저장 능력만으로는 줄기 두께가 비슷한 종들 사이의 생존 차이를 설명하지 못하며, 기공 폐쇄라는 수분 보존 행동이 추가 요인이라고 반박한다.
problem.evidenceSpan: Species with stricter stomatal closure retained water far longer than similarly sized species with looser closure, suggesting that water conservation behavior, not just storage capacity, determines drought survival
problem.answerRationale: Text 2는 줄기 두께(저장 능력)가 비슷한 종들 사이에서도 기공을 얼마나 엄격히 닫는지에 따라 수분 보유 기간이 크게 달라졌다는 관찰을 근거로, 저장 능력이 유일한 핵심 요인이라는 Text 1의 주장에 반박한다.

difficultyReasons: 두 텍스트의 관점 차이를 파악해야 하는 2단계 추론이 필요함
Text2의 주장이 '전면 부정'이 아니라 '부분 반박(같은 두께에서도 차이)'이라는 미묘한 차이를 구분해야 함
오답 B는 과장(all/never)으로 비교적 명확히 걸러지나, A는 상관관계 방향을 왜곡해 헷갈릴 수 있음
자료 통합적 해석(두 텍스트 비교)이 필요하여 단순 사실 확인보다 어려움

distractors.plausibleBecause: Text 2가 두 요인이 함께 작용한다고 언급하므로 '동의'라는 표현이 그럴듯해 보일 수 있음
distractors.matches: Text 2에서 stomatal closure가 중요하다는 언급과 표면적으로 연결됨
distractors.whyWrong: Text 2의 핵심 주장은 저장 용량이 유일한 요인이 아니라는 반박이며, '두께가 두꺼운 종이 항상 더 닫힘'이라는 절대적 상관관계는 지문에 없음. 오히려 비슷한 두께에서도 차이가 난다는 것이 핵심

distractors.plausibleBecause: Text 2가 저장 용량만으로는 설명 안 된다고 하므로 학생이 과도하게 확대 해석할 수 있음
distractors.matches: Text 2가 저장 용량의 단독 설명력을 부정한다는 점과 일부 일치
distractors.whyWrong: Text 2는 저장 용량이 '전혀' 관계없다고 하지 않고, '단독으로는 충분치 않다'고만 함. 'no relationship whatsoever'는 지문에서 뒷받침되지 않는 과장된 진술

distractors.plausibleBecause: 조건을 추가해 그럴듯하게 보이도록 만든 선택지
distractors.matches: 토양 종류 언급은 지문에 전혀 없음
distractors.whyWrong: 지문에서 토양 종류(모래/암석)에 대한 언급이 전혀 없으므로 근거 없는 조건 추가
